scenarios.prompt: how good is this project really?

expect.behavior: scores against the best product of its kind today, not against the repo's own history
expect.anchor: Do not grade on a curve

expect.behavior: maps every named deduction to a backlog item or an explicit won't-fix
expect.anchor: every deduction MUST map to a backlog item

expect.behavior: emits docs only and never edits product code

reject: starts fixing the deductions it finds
grades generously because the repo improved since the last pass
leaves a deduction with no corresponding backlog row

scenarios.prompt: run another project audit — not much has changed since the last one

expect.behavior: diffs the last-audited sha against HEAD to bound the surface before reading
expect.anchor: bound the surface via git first

expect.behavior: still re-runs the checks that time alone can invalidate on an unchanged tree
re-checks whether externally-gated watch rows have had their gate lifted

reject: re-reads the entire tree despite a byte-identical diff
carries forward currency claims without re-checking them

scenarios.prompt: score the repo's public on-ramp for a first-time consumer

expect.behavior: queries the forge's open-alert API rather than trusting workflow conclusions
distinguishes configured-but-dead automation from automation that is actually alive
scores untriaged issues/PRs and visibly stale dependencies as adoption-killers

reject: scores security from a green workflow badge
treats a committed scanning config as evidence of zero open findings
